patch.objective: Explain dermatomes, and how damage to one spinal nerve root produces sensory loss over that root's dermatome
secondaryObjectives: Distinguish the central and peripheral nervous systems, the somatic and autonomic divisions, and afferent (sensory) from efferent (motor) pathways

sources.cite: Lumen Learning, Anatomy and Physiology (SUNY Dutchess), 'Spinal Nerves' (adapted from sources including OpenStax Anatomy & Physiology, CC BY)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: 'The region of the skin that each spinal nerve carries information from is called its dermatome'; a dermatome map helps locate an injury. The page does not mention the cauda equina and could not be confirmed as OpenStax text. The case's red flags (saddle numbness, new bladder change) are the sacral roots' dermatomes and autonomic outflow, which is why they are reported at once.

sources.cite: House of Delegates policy HOD P06-18-28-35, Direction and Supervision of the Physical Therapist Assistant (last updated 2018-08-30)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch with quotes. Only the physical therapist performs 'Evaluation, diagnosis, and prognosis', the initial examination and reexamination, and the 'Development or modification of a plan of care'; the PTA may be used in 'collection of selected examination and outcomes data' and 'makes modifications to elements of the intervention either to progress the patient or client as directed by the physical therapist or to ensure patient or client safety and comfort'. A PT supervisory visit is made 'upon the physical therapist assistant's request for a reexamination' and 'in response to a change in the patient's or client's medical status'.

sources.cite: Margetis K, et al. Low Back Pain: Evaluation and Management. StatPearls (updated 2025-12-13), StatPearls Publishing
sources.note: Relayed from the course seed's source list (tag SP-LBP; read 2026-11-04 from NCBI's StatPearls literature-archive snapshot), not re-read: new urinary retention, bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia or bilateral leg weakness is possible cauda equina syndrome, a surgical emergency; red flags for cancer, infection and fracture are screening prompts.
Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated model. The pace of the compression and the effect of traction are authored and carry FLAG.
